text:
Eli: Hi team, opened my first PR touching runtime/scheduler to tweak batch timeout. Branch: feat/eli/batch-timeout-adjust. Two quick Qs: 1) do we require signed commits? 2) what's the preferred merge strategy for small runtime tweaks?

Tara: Welcome Eli! We prefer signed commits for security-sensitive repos, runtime included. Use `git commit -S` or configure gpg/ssh signing. If you can't sign yet, add a comment and we'll approve but it's good to enable.

Mateo: Merge strategy: small fixes -> squash; behavior changes -> merge commit. For anything that affects scheduling, add an entry in the runtime changelog under docs/release-notes/draft.md.

Eli: thanks. I tried `git commit -S` but my key isn't recognized in CI. Any tips?

Tara: Make sure your public key is uploaded to your GitHub account and that `gpg --list-secret-keys` shows the key. CI checks signature verification via `git log --show-signature -1`. If you're blocked, ping security and add `[unsigned]` to the PR body for now.

ops-bot: Please note: runtime repo requires at least 1 infra reviewer when touching /scheduler or /placement. CODEOWNERS will request @Mateo automatically for /runtime/scheduler/*

Eli: I also want to follow the branch naming convention. I used feat/eli/batch-timeout-adjust. Is that okay?

Mateo: That's fine but prefer feat/runtime/<short>. So feat/runtime/eli/batch-timeout-adjust helps searches. Not mandatory but recommended.

ci-bot: CI queued for feat/eli/batch-timeout-adjust — build 4891 — tests: unit, linters, integration-slim

Lina: One more note about PR content: include a short test plan and rollout steps in the PR body. Example: how to validate on staging, flags to toggle, and metrics to watch (queue_latency_ms).

Eli: Good call. I added a test plan: ran unit + scheduler sim locally, toggled feature flag locally, and will deploy to staging; will watch queue_latency_ms and gpu_util.

Mateo: Also, if you touch runtime config, add `config/schema` validation in CI by including schema changes or bumping schema version. We have a blocker job that fails if schema mismatch is detected.

Eli: CI failed on a lint: yaml spacing in scheduler config. Is auto-fix preferred or should I leave it for the reviewer?

Tara: Auto-fix and force-push is fine for formatting. Run `prettier --write` and `ruff --fix`. For config schema changes, add a one-line note in the PR body.

Eli: Fixed formatting and pushed. CI now failing on a flaky test integration/scheduler/throughput_test — timed out. Any guidance?

Mateo: Re-run the flaky job. If it repros, label `test/investigate`. We have a weekly flaky grooming board. If your change is unrelated, sometimes re-run passes.

Eli: Re-run passed. Requested reviewers @Mateo and @Tara. Also added changelog bullet and test plan.

Tara: Looks good. One tiny process note: when you want this cherry-picked to the current release branch, add `cherry/this-release` label and request a release-assist from the releases channel.

Eli: Noted. Appreciate the quick onboarding help!

Mateo: Welcome aboard Eli :wave: If you're curious about branching history policy (rebase vs merge), ping me and I'll share a short doc.

Eli: Will do — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
